description: Consumer VPN service known for beginner-friendly apps and playful bear branding; owned by McAfee. Its affiliate program pays a flat percentage on every subscription plan sold through a referral link, with no minimum payout.

evidence.summary: TunnelBear's own affiliate page (fetched directly) states 'There's no limit on how much you can earn!' and 'No minimums — get paid every month, whether it's $10 or $10,000.' The page's join links route to Impact (app.impact.com). No commission percentage is stated on the brand's own page.

Lasso's program profile and VPN roundup list TunnelBear at 50% per sale via Impact (Impact Radius) with a $50 payout threshold; several independent VPN affiliate roundups agree on the 50% rate. Cookie length varies between listings (30 vs 45 days). One directory (Shopper) claims 70% and was treated as unreliable boilerplate.

name: TunnelBear

opportunity.notes: Verified uncapped: the brand's own affiliate page explicitly says there is no limit on how much an affiliate can earn, and there is no minimum payout. Applications run through Impact. No published creator-count or small-creator policy was found, so saturation is recorded unknown.

reasons: Verified uncapped on the brand's own affiliate page ('There's no limit on how much you can earn!') with a 50% per-sale rate via Impact — top compensation profile in this group.
Consumer VPN is a natural fit for tech, privacy and travel creator content, and the brand's friendly positioning demos well on video.
No public program email was found on the affiliate page, so contact access is limited to the Impact application.

description: Consumer VPN service selling monthly, annual and multi-year plans. Its in-house affiliate program pays 100% commission on monthly-plan signups, 40% on other plans, and 35% recurring lifetime commissions, with a $300 signup bonus.

evidence.summary: PureVPN's own affiliate page (fetched directly) states 100% commission on monthly-plan new signups, 40% on other plans, 35% recurring lifetime commissions, a 90-day cookie and a $300 signup bonus, and publishes partners@purevpn.com. Its earnings copy ('sky's the limit') is vague marketing with no explicit no-cap statement, so the cap is recorded unknown.

name: PureVPN

opportunity.notes: In-house program applied to from the brand's own affiliate page. The 100% headline rate applies to monthly-plan new signups only; other plans pay 40% and renewals pay 35% recurring. No explicit earnings-cap statement and no published creator-count data were found.

reasons: Among the highest published VPN rates anywhere: 100% on monthly plans, 40% on other plans, 35% recurring, plus a $300 signup bonus — all from the brand's own page.
A direct program contact (partners@purevpn.com) is published on the affiliate page.
Cap is honestly unknown: the page's 'sky's the limit' line is marketing language, not an explicit no-cap statement.

description: All-in-one workspace app with a large creator and template-maker community. Its affiliate program explicitly welcomes content creators and influencers, paying up to $50 per activated paid sign-up plus 20% of first-year revenue, tracked through PartnerStack.

evidence.summary: Notion's own affiliates page (fetched directly) states: 'Earn commissions up to $50 per activated sign up plus 20% of year one revenue for each referral you drive', tracked through PartnerStack, and lists 'Content creators & influencers' as an eligible audience. Older third-party listings citing 50% of first-year payments describe a previous structure and conflict with the current page, so the mixed flat-plus-revenue-share structure is recorded with a null percentage rate.

The same page explains that conversions are net-new workspaces upgrading to a paid Plus or Business plan within 180 days of the click, links are managed in the PartnerStack dashboard, and promotions must be FTC-disclosed.

name: Notion

opportunity.notes: One of the most creator-native programs in this group: the brand's own page names content creators, influencers and template creators as target applicants and provides an Affiliates Resource Center. Pay is a flat bounty (up to $50 per activated sign-up) plus 20% of year-one revenue, so no single percentage rate is recorded. No cap statement or creator-count data was published.

reasons: Explicitly built for creators: the program page lists content creators and influencers as eligible and supports them with a resource center — exceptional UGC evidence.
Productivity and template content is a proven short-form niche, giving the program top niche fit for this group.
Compensation is a hybrid (up to $50 flat per activated sign-up plus 20% of year-one revenue) rather than a high percentage, and older 50% listings conflict with the current page.

description: Consumer data-recovery, backup and partition software for Windows and Mac. EaseUS runs an affiliate program (30% default, up to 60%) across several networks and a separate creator program paying up to 50%.

evidence.summary: EaseUS's official partner page advertises up to 60% commission and publishes affiliate@easeus.com; program listings citing the official page put the default rate at 30%. The program is carried on multiple networks (Impact, CJ, Partnerize), and a FlexOffers listing shows 40%, so the recorded rate is the 30% default.
EaseUS also runs a dedicated creator program on its own domain paying up to 50%, separate from the standard affiliate program.

name: EaseUS

opportunity.notes: Two doors in: the standard affiliate program (30% default, up to 60%, multi-network) and a dedicated creator program paying up to 50%. Rates vary by network and product, so the default 30% is recorded. No cap statement or creator-count data was published.

reasons: A dedicated creator program (up to 50%) on top of the standard affiliate program is strong creator evidence for a software brand.
Published program contact (affiliate@easeus.com) and multiple network doors make access straightforward.
Headline 'up to 60%' is a ceiling, not the default; the recorded 30% default keeps compensation scoring honest.

description: Consumer creative and utility software maker (Filmora video editor, UniConverter, PDFelement). Its affiliate program pays tiered commissions starting at 30% and rising to 50% based on quarterly sales volume.

evidence.summary: Wondershare's own affiliate pages describe tiered commissions starting at 30% for lower quarterly sales and rising to 50% at the highest tier, and publish affiliate@wondershare.com for the program. Listings place the program on CJ, Impact, ShareASale, Awin and LinkConnector; CJ is recorded as the primary network.

name: Wondershare

opportunity.notes: Filmora is itself a creator tool, so the product is unusually demonstrable for video creators. Entry tier is 30%; the 50% top tier requires very high quarterly sales. No cap statement or creator-count data was published.

reasons: Creator-tool products (Filmora, UniConverter) are natively demonstrable in short-form video.
Solid 30% entry tier across several major networks, with a published program contact.
The 50% headline is a high-volume tier, so compensation is scored on the 30% entry rate.

description: Password manager from the Nord Security team behind NordVPN. Its in-house affiliate program pays 30% on new B2C sign-ups and 10% on renewals, with a $100 minimum payout.

evidence.summary: NordPass's own affiliate pages state B2C commissions of 30% on new sign-ups and 10% on renewals (B2B new sign-ups 25%), run as an in-house program with a $100 payout minimum. A Lasso roundup claiming 75% conflicts with the brand's own published structure and was not used.

name: NordPass

opportunity.notes: In-house program applied to from the brand's own affiliate page; renewals keep paying at 10%, which suits evergreen password-security content. A third-party 75% claim conflicts with the brand's own pages and was discarded. No cap statement or creator-count data was published.

reasons: Backed by the Nord Security brand, giving it top credibility in this group.
30% on new sign-ups plus 10% recurring on renewals is a fair, clearly published structure from the brand's own pages.
No public program email was recorded and the $100 payout minimum slows first earnings for small creators.

description: Long-running consumer password manager by Siber Systems. Its affiliate program pays 30% revenue share on new Premium subscriptions (renewals excluded).

evidence.summary: RoboForm's own affiliates page states 30% revenue share on new Premium subscriptions (renewals excluded) and publishes the program contact affiliates@sibersystems.zendesk.com. Tracking-network attribution conflicts between listings (Everflow in a listing validated 2026-11-09 vs CJ in another), so Everflow is recorded and the conflict is noted here.

name: RoboForm

opportunity.notes: Established password-manager brand with a clearly published 30% rate and program contact on its own page. Renewals earn nothing, and the tracking network should be confirmed at application because listings conflict (Everflow vs CJ). No cap statement or creator-count data was published.

reasons: Clean 30% revenue share stated on the brand's own affiliates page, with a published program contact.
Password managers are a crowded creator niche (NordPass is in this same group), trimming niche fit.
No renewal commissions and a network-attribution conflict between listings keep the score mid-pack.

description: US pet insurance provider for dogs and cats. Its affiliate program pays a flat $36 bounty per qualified lead with a long 180-day cookie, a fit for pet creators making insurance and pet-cost content.

evidence.summary: Backlinko's affiliate program directory lists Embrace Pet Insurance at a flat $36 per lead with a 180-day cookie, and Strackr's program guide agrees on the $36 flat lead bounty. Network attribution conflicts between listings (Strackr places it on FlexOffers; UpPromote's directory lists Impact), so FlexOffers is recorded and the conflict should be confirmed at application.

name: Embrace Pet Insurance

opportunity.notes: Flat $36 per lead (not per sale) is unusually creator-friendly for pet content, since a quote request earns without a purchase. The rate is a flat bounty, so no percentage is recorded. Confirm the tracking network at application — listings conflict between FlexOffers and Impact. No cap statement or creator-count data was published.

reasons: A flat $36 per lead with a 180-day cookie pays on quote requests, not just completed purchases — strong economics for pet-cost content.
Established, well-reviewed US pet insurer, giving it top credibility in this group.
Evidence is listing-based rather than a fetched brand program page, and the network attribution conflicts between sources.

description: Online pet pharmacy selling pet medications and supplies. Its affiliate program runs on CJ Affiliate and pays 8% per sale with a 45-day cookie.

evidence.summary: Lasso's Allivet program profile lists the program on CJ Affiliate at 8% per sale with a 45-day cookie. A Shopper directory entry citing 5-10% could not be verified against its own source and was not used.

name: Allivet

opportunity.notes: Pet pharmacy is an everyday-purchase niche that suits routine-care content. The 8% CJ rate is modest, and program evidence is listing-based. No cap statement or creator-count data was published.

reasons: Repeat-purchase pet pharmacy products fit routine pet-care content well.
8% per sale via CJ is workable but modest next to this group's software rates.
Listing-based evidence only; no brand program page or public contact was verified.

description: Maker of Instant Pot multi-cookers and other Instant kitchen appliances, now trading as Instant Pot Brands after a 2023 Chapter 11 restructuring. An affiliate program exists, but published rates and management conflict across sources, so terms must be confirmed at application.

evidence.summary: Published Instant Brands affiliate terms conflict sharply: Lasso's current profile lists 4% per sale (45-day cookie), LinkClicky lists 1% per sale on CJ Affiliate (March 2024), AdCompares lists a flat 3% managed directly by Gen3 Marketing, and an older Refersion profile cited 8%. Because the rate and even the managing network conflict, the commission rate is recorded null. Sovrn's merchant page also notes that, following the 2023 restructuring, current affiliate availability has not been independently verified — confirm live terms before promoting.

name: Instant Brands

opportunity.notes: Instant Pot is one of the most demonstrable kitchen brands on video, but this entry is flagged needs_review: rates conflict (1% / 3% / 4% / 8%) and management attribution conflicts (CJ vs Gen3 Marketing vs an older Refersion profile), and the company restructured out of Chapter 11 in 2023-2024. Verify the live program and rate inside the network before creating content.

reasons: Instant Pot demos exceptionally well in recipe and kitchen content, keeping niche fit respectable despite the weak terms.
Rate is recorded null: published figures conflict across four sources (1%, 3%, 4%, 8%).
Post-bankruptcy restructuring and unverified current merchant status (per Sovrn) cap credibility and availability scores until terms are confirmed live.
